newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil notifies ACPC it has exceeded coffee quota.
newsitem.headline: Brazil notifies ACPC it has exceeded coffee quota.

text.p: Brazil has officially notified the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) that it has overshot its target of coffee exports in the first half of 1997, a top government commodity official said.

"We sent them an official communique that there was this increase but that it was very positive for international markets," Mauricio Assis, head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department, told reporters.
Assis was talking to reporters at a coffee fair in Sao Paulo.
Under an ACPC agreement, Brazil should not have shipped more than six million bags between January and June this year.
However by end-May, exports had reached 6.46 million bags, with some traders also expecting sizeable shipments this month.

The larger-than-expected shipments are because all private stocks have all been sold, the soluble industry has exported less and producers have also taken advantage of high international prices, Assis said.
Other producing countries were also likely to sell more than their quota given attractive world prices, he added.
